subject: AuroraData marketplace metering & co-sell ops question
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Patel <aaron@auroradata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: AuroraData listing — metering clarification before co-sell sign-off

Aaron —

Thanks again for the productive walkthrough on Friday. We ran the listing checklist with the marketplace team this morning and a couple of metering/sku items came up that we should resolve before we request the co-sell badge:

1) SKU granularity: your current SKU bundle maps a single SKU to both hosted inference and dedicated deployments. Marketplace catalog rules expect separate SKUs (or flags) for hosted vs. managed/private offers so billing attribution doesn't conflate Redwood-hosted consumption with partner-managed instances. Can you confirm whether AuroraData wants two SKUs or a single SKU with usage-type labels?

2) Trial egress credits: the GCP private offer folks asked how trial egress credits will be applied and whether they require an AMI-level entitlement. If AuroraData wants credits to flow back to Redwood for co-sell uplift calculation, we need an explicit line item.

3) Co-sell revshare baseline: Vivek and I need to confirm the baseline commitment (monthly minimum) you expect before co-sell uplift kicks in. We can model two scenarios but will need the preferred number to complete the mutual action plan.

I attached the evidence binder we pulled together and a draft SKU mapping (v2) that highlights the ambiguities. If you can comment inline by EOD Wednesday we can lock this and move to marketplace intake.

Next steps I propose:
- AuroraData to confirm SKU approach (two SKUs vs labels)
- AuroraData to confirm trial egress credit flow
- Redwood (Vivek/Ben) to model revshare waterfall once we have baseline

Thanks — short on the ask so we can keep the intake window open.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Head of Partnerships (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: auroradata-evidence-binder.pdf, auroradata-sku-mapping-v2.xlsx
From: Aaron Patel <aaron@auroradata.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@auroradata.com>, partnerships@auroradata.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraData listing — metering clarification before co-sell sign-off

Avery —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers below, plus a note on implementation:

1) SKU granularity — We prefer two SKUs: AD-CORE-HOSTED and AD-CORE-MGR (managed). The hosted SKU will be the default in Redwood's hosted offering; managed will be used for Aurora-managed private instances. We'll update the SKU sheet accordingly.

2) Trial egress credits — We do want credits to show as a separate line item that can be attributed to Redwood for uplift. Our finance team will draft language that specifies credit redemption rules (expiry, limits).

3) Revshare baseline — Our initial ask is a $12k/month baseline for the first 6 months, with 5% uplift thereafter tied to co-sell-sourced bookings. If that is a blocker, tell us what Redwood would model for a lower baseline, and we'll iterate.

I'll loop Priya and our finance contact if we need to provide an updated price sheet. Expect us to return the annotated SKU mapping by Wednesday EOD PST.

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Patel
Head of Cloud Partnerships
AuroraData
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: AuroraData listing — metering clarification before co-sell sign-off

Looping in a couple of quick ops constraints I ran into when I tried to map AD-CORE-HOSTED to our metering tables:

- Marketplace metering expects a consumption dimension (tokens / inference-minutes) rather than a blended SKU for all token types. If AuroraData's hosted SKU will be per-token it needs a clear token definition (prompt vs completion vs embedding).

- For managed/private deployments the metering key must be tied to the partner-managed subscription id so cloud marketplace reports attribute usage correctly to the partner account. That means AD-CORE-MGR should be provisioned as a partner-managed offer in the portal (we can't partition a Redwood-hosted SKU and treat parts as partner-managed later).

If AuroraData can provide the token type mapping and confirm partner-managed offer intent we can finalize the SKU mapping and push to intake. Also, Vivek: for the revshare modeling I assumed a 3-tier waterfall (baseline -> co-sell uplift -> acceleration) and did a quick scenario for $12k baseline; shared the calc in the Drive link.

-Ben

P.S. Avery — if AuroraData insists on a single SKU with labels we can support it but it will add a reconciliation step each month which complicates co-sell % attribution. Worth flagging to them as a friction point.
From: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@auroradata.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron@auroradata.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraData listing — metering clarification before co-sell sign-off

Hi all —

Thanks for the notes. We've updated the SKU sheet and uploaded a short FAQ on credit handling (see attached pages 3-4 in the evidence binder). Key confirmations:

- We will publish two SKUs (AD-CORE-HOSTED, AD-CORE-MGR). Hosted will meter by token-type: prompt_token, completion_token, embedding_token. Definitions are in the attached workbook.

- Trial egress credits will be a separate line item that Redwood can include in co-sell attribution. Credits expire after 90 days and are capped at $1,000 per trial account.

- Baseline: AuroraData is comfortable testing with Redwood's modeled lower baseline of $8k/month for Q3 as a compromise; if co-sell-sourced bookings exceed $30k in a quarter, uplift increases to 5% retroactively.

Action items we need from Redwood to complete intake:
1) Ben/Vivek to confirm marketplace offer type for managed SKU (partner-managed vs reseller).
2) Soojin to confirm whether Redwood's co-sell telemetry will accept token-level metering as a primary input for uplift calculations (we've seen mismatches before when using blended metrics).
3) Avery to kick off the intake ticket once items 1-2 are clear — target intake submission Friday PDT.

We'll mark up the Drive doc with the final SKU IDs by EOD Friday.

Best,
Priya Mehta
Partnerships & Marketplace Ops
AuroraData
